tools.why: Enables `:Case ocr` — reading the text out of a case's screenshots into searchable sidecar files. Runs through images.nvim's OCR module, so both have to be present. Language data beyond English is a separate package per language (tesseract-ocr-deu and friends). On Windows the UB-Mannheim installer does not add itself to PATH; images.nvim probes the usual install directory anyway, or set its `ocr.bin`.

Converts a case bundle to standalone HTML on the way to `:Case export`'s PDF, which a headless Chrome/Edge then prints. Without it the export reports the missing tool and stops — there is no second conversion path.
Lets lazygit open a file in *this* Neovim instance instead of starting a nested one — without it, editing a file from inside the lazygit terminal traps you in an editor inside an editor.
Syntax-highlights the file preview in the harpoon fzf menu. Purely cosmetic: without it the preview falls back to plain `cat`-style output.
Bridges the Neovim clipboard to the Windows clipboard from inside WSL. Only relevant there; a native Windows or Linux session uses its own provider and never looks for this.
Provides the clipboard under Wayland (both halves ship in one package, wl-clipboard). Without it, yanking to `+`/`*` silently does nothing on a Wayland session. Irrelevant on X11, Windows and macOS.
